title: Lock out a machine's START push button with a push-button lockout cover and padlock
instruction: Lock out the green START button with the clear push-button cover: take the open cover from the block on the right, set it around the START button so its bottom edge goes under the clear base ring, close the cover, then put the blue padlock's shackle through both of the cover's ears and snap it shut. Do not press either button, and do not cover the red STOP button.
context: A padlocked cover over a machine's START button keeps anyone from starting it while a worker clears a jam or cleans it; it is applied together with isolating the machine's energy. Pressing START while fitting the cover would start the machine, covering STOP would keep anyone from stopping it, and a cover that is closed but not padlocked can simply be opened.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Push-button station: a light-grey (RAL 7035) steel push-button enclosure, 19 x 14.5 cm and 9.75 cm tall, lies on the table fixed to it, spanning 12 to 31 cm in front of the bases and 0.5 to 15 cm right of the midline, its top face up. Two 22 mm flush spring-return push buttons stand on the top face, 7.5 cm right of the midline: a green START (Schneider XB4BA31, 1 NO) 19 cm in front of the bases and a red STOP (XB4BA42, 1 NC) 26 cm in front; each has a chrome bezel 30 mm across standing 9 mm proud of the top and a flush cap that travels 4.3 mm (contact at 2.6 mm, 3.8 N). A black legend plate (40 x 14 mm, white text START / STOP) lies on the top face 6.3 cm right of each button's axis. Under each bezel is a clear Master Lock S2152AST install base: a flat ring 60.4 mm across with a 5 mm tall rim around its edge. Cover: a clear polycarbonate Master Lock S2151 removable push-button cover (64.4 mm across, 50 mm tall, 1.8 mm walls, 36 g): two half-shells on a vertical hinge whose knuckles face the robot's right; at the other seam, facing left, each half has a padlock ear (a 14 x 18 mm plate, 2.5 mm thick, with a 9 mm hole 6 mm above the cover's top; shut, the two ears lie face to face). It stands open by 30 degrees (the half nearer the robot swung open) on a grey steel block 12 x 12 cm, 5.25 cm tall, centred 22 cm in front of the bases and 22.5 cm right of the midline, its axis over the block's centre. Padlock: a blue Master Lock 410BLU Zenex padlock (thermoplastic body 38 x 19 x 44 mm, 6.35 mm steel shackle, 38 mm vertical clearance, 100 g), unlocked with its shackle popped up 16 mm, lies level on its 38 x 44 mm face, shackle pointing right toward the station, body centred 19 cm in front of the bases, 7 cm left of the midline and 15.35 cm above the table, on a grey steel pedestal (a 1.2 x 1.6 cm column on a 5 x 5 x 1 cm foot) whose 3.8 x 2.2 cm top, 14.35 cm above the table, carries only the shackle end of the body. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if either button's cap is ever pushed in 2.6 mm or more (its contact point), or if the cover is ever set over the STOP button (its axis within 1.5 cm of the STOP's axis and its bottom within 1.5 cm of the top face). Otherwise the score is the highest level reached. 0.25: the cover stands around the START button: its axis within 2.5 mm of the button's axis, upright within 5 degrees, its bottom edge within 3 mm of the top face. 0.5: as for 0.25, with the cover shut (its halves within 3 degrees of closed). 0.75: as for 0.5, with the padlock's shackle snapped shut through both ears' holes. 1.0: as for 0.75, and the after-release check passes. After-release check, once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the padlock's body and 7 cm from the cover's centre for 1 s (if they never are, the check is not done and the score is at most 0.75), each load held 1.5 s with a spring scale: (1) press the cover's top down over the button with 20 N: passes if the START cap moves in less than 1 mm; (2) holding one half, pull the other half's ear outward with 5 N (0.35 N m about the hinge): passes if the cover opens less than 10 degrees; (3) lift the cover straight up with 10 N: passes if it rises less than 3 mm. A padlocked cover that fails any check stays at 0.75. Distances are measured with a rule, angles from a photo with a protractor, button travel with a depth gauge or the contact's continuity (battery tester).
reset_notes: Unlock the padlock with its key, take it off the ears, close its shackle to the popped-up position and lay it back on the pedestal, shackle toward the station. Open the cover, lift it off the base and stand it on the block open by 30 degrees, hinge to the right, ears to the left. Check both buttons spring back fully. About 1 minute. For real trials the station's contacts are not wired to a machine; if button presses are to be logged, wire each contact to a battery continuity tester.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, station arm gains. Geometry holds: the shut cover's bottom lips sit under the base's rim, it encloses the button with 38 mm clearance, a shackle through both ears stops it opening. Published: button travel and force, cover button-size range, 410 outline. Inferred: cover and base dimensions, lip, ears. Rules: button spring, shackle latch; checks applied after recording. Details in README.
